LOS ANGELES, November 04, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Tutor Perini Corporation (NYSE: TPC), a leading civil, building and specialty construction company, announced today that its Board of Directors has declared a quarterly cash dividend in the amount of $0.09 per share of Tutor Perini common stock payable on December 3, 2026, to shareholders of record as of the close of business on November 19, 2026.

About Tutor Perini Corporation

Tutor Perini Corporation is a leading civil, building and specialty construction company offering diversified general contracting and design-build services to private customers and public agencies throughout the world. We have provided construction services since 1894 and have established a strong reputation within our markets by executing large, complex projects on time and within budget while adhering to strict safety and quality control measures. We offer general contracting, pre-construction planning and comprehensive project management services, and have strong expertise in delivering design-bid-build, design-build, construction management, and public-private partnership (P3) projects. We often self-perform multiple project components, including earthwork, excavation, concrete forming and placement, steel erection, electrical, mechanical, plumbing, heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC), and fire protection.

Retirement changes how income works. Paychecks stop, but property taxes, groceries, and Medicare premiums keep arriving on schedule. For investors at or near that point, the useful question is how much reliable cash a portfolio can produce without selling shares.

A $50,000 stake in each of these five dividend payers would generate the following. The group includes two telecoms, two tobacco makers and an integrated oil major, and each has paid quarterly dividends for decades. All yields below are forward yields: the annualized dividend divided by the current share price.

Philip Morris International: Smoke-Free Growth Funds a Bigger Payout

Philip Morris sells Marlboro and local cigarette brands outside the U.S. Smoke-free products such as IQOS and ZYN now make up more than 40% of its revenue. Adjusted EPS guidance of $8.29 to $8.44 for 2026 covers the $6.40 annualized dividend. At the low end of guidance, the payout ratio is about 77%. The board raised the quarterly dividend 8.8% to $1.60, and net debt to adjusted EBITDA fell to 2.17x.

Investing.com -- AT&T looks like the most vulnerable U.S. carrier if SpaceX turns Starlink into a full mobile network.

Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list »

AT&T faces the most pressure

AT&T Inc (T) has the weakest current EBITDA margin of the three at 35.7%, versus 37.4% for Verizon Communications Inc (VZ) and 37.7% for T-Mobile US Inc (TMUS). Its debt-to-EBITDA is also high at 3.5x, as of Sep 30, 2026.

Why AT&T

Strategic gap: T-Mobile already has a commercial satellite relationship with Starlink. That makes T-Mobile US Inc (TMUS) both a potential rival and an early beneficiary.

AT&T and Verizon opposed higher-power Starlink direct-to-cell operations, while T-Mobile had already begun testing the service. That gives T-Mobile more time to adapt its customer proposition. Read more (Mar 7, 2025)

Balance-sheet sensitivity: SpaceX would pressure rural coverage, secondary-market pricing and network differentiation. AT&T has less financial flexibility than T-Mobile, with $180.61B of debt versus $118.99B for T-Mobile, as of Sep 30, 2026.

The important twist

Verizon is not safe. It has the largest debt load at $195.29B, as of Sep 30, 2026. However, its scale, network density and enterprise relationships provide stronger defenses.

Unsure what to buy ahead of earnings? Our AI's recent pre-earnings calls delivered gains of +77% to +118% after results dropped. See this month's earnings picks »

T-Mobile is the paradox. It suffered the sharpest initial market reaction—about 10% in the Oct 9, 2026 coverage—but its Starlink partnership may also provide the best defensive head start. Read more (Oct 9, 2026)

SpaceX's threat is becoming more credible because it combines low-band spectrum, satellites and a reported plan to access up to 80,000 U.S. cell sites. That is closer to a fourth carrier than a rural coverage add-on. Read more (Oct 23, 2026)

Bottom line

Most vulnerable: AT&T Inc (T).

The reasoning is not that AT&T has the weakest network. It is that SpaceX could attack its coverage and pricing model while AT&T carries heavy debt and lacks T-Mobile's direct satellite head start.

Bull case: SpaceX remains capacity-constrained and becomes a partner rather than a full substitute.

Bear case: satellite coverage plus selective terrestrial sites erodes the value of nationwide carrier exclusivity.

title: At 70 He’ll Get a Letter Saying His Company Is Handing His Pension to an Insurance Company. The Check Stays the Same, but the Federal Safety Net Behind It Doesn’t

At 70 He’ll Get a Letter Saying His Company Is Handing His Pension to an Insurance Company. The Check Stays the Same, but the Federal Safety Net Behind It Doesn’t

Quick Read

When employers transfer pensions to insurers, federal PBGC protection disappears and state guaranty associations take over, covering only $100,000 to $500,000 in annuity present value.

A $2,000 monthly pension paid over 15 years is worth roughly $249,000, putting it right at most states' $250,000 coverage cap before any survivor benefit is added.

Retirees should verify the insurer's financial strength ratings, confirm all benefit terms match exactly, and check whether their state's guaranty association fully covers their pension's present value.

Building a portfolio and living off one are two completely different skills, and almost nobody teaches the second. This problem is what The Definitive Guide to Retirement Income helps, and it is free today. Read more here. (Sponsor)

He read the letter twice before realizing that his old employer is moving his pension to an insurance company, but the monthly amount isn't changing. That part was a relief, even though the letter didn't explain what else was changing. The answer is in the fine print about who stands behind the check.

shapecharge from Getty Images Signature and designer491 from Getty Images

Lots of retirees will get this same letter. Households 70 and older held about $4.8 trillion in traditional pension benefits in the second quarter of 2026. That's a record 26% of the U.S. total, according to Federal Reserve data.

Why Your Old Employer Wants Out of the Pension Business

The company pays an insurer a lump sum to buy a group annuity, a contract in which the insurer promises to send everyone's checks for life. The industry calls this a pension risk transfer. In 2012, General Motors (NYSE:GM) and Verizon (NYSE:VZ) did it with Prudential (NYSE:PRU), and many big employers have followed. Full-year 2025 premiums were estimated at about $48 billion, and one insurer tracking the market projects $35 billion to $40 billion for 2026.

title: Amdocs: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
detail:
Amdocs: 3 Key Takeaways for Long-Term Investors
The Motley Fool Team, The Motley Fool
Wed, November 4, 2026 at 8:16 AM MST 3 min read
DOX
T
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

On its fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 3, 2026, Amdocs (NASDAQ:DOX) announced an 8-year strategic agreement with AT&T to deploy its new artificial intelligence software platform. The update reveals how the provider of managed services, multiyear contracts where the company runs customer billing and IT operations, is navigating customer concentration risks. Three things management said stand out.

1. AT&T Signs 8-Year Deal for Amdocs Agentic Operating System

The long-term agreement with its largest customer validates the new Amdocs Agentic Operating System (AOS), a software platform that automates complex telecom operations using artificial intelligence agents.

We signed an 8-year strategic agreement with AT&T, our largest customer. The strategic agreement is designed to accelerate the transformation of their business by adopting our agentic technology in combination with AT&T's leading AI capabilities.
-- Shimie Hortig, President and Chief Executive Officer

2. Amdocs Diversifies Into Insurance With the Acquisition of EIS

To expand beyond its core telecommunications market, the business purchased EIS, a provider of core software platforms for insurance carriers, to establish a second major growth engine.

Executing on our strategy, I'm pleased to announce today that Amdocs has acquired EIS for $340 million in cash. EIS is a leading provider of agentic insurance core systems platforms spanning policy, billing, claims and customer engagement.
-- Shimie Hortig, President and Chief Executive Officer

3. T-Mobile Legal Dispute Triggers Significant Fiscal 2027 Revenue Decline

A legal conflict with T-Mobile, a key customer, forced management to issue conservative guidance expecting fiscal 2027 revenue to shrink despite mid-single-digit expansion across the rest of the business.

At the same time, we are facing major headwinds due to the situation we have with T-Mobile. This is an isolated situation with a large customer, resulting in a significant decline in our revenue and profitability outlook for next year.
-- Shimie Hortig, President and Chief Executive Officer

Looking Ahead

Growth outside the T-Mobile relationship continues, supported by long-term customer commitments and deep operational integration. Management is tracking contract dispute developments and expansion into insurance software.

Outside of T-Mobile, the rest of Amdocs' business is robust and expected to grow mid-single digits in fiscal 2027.
-- Shimie Hortig, President and Chief Executive Officer

title: If AT&T's Debt Stays High, What Happens To Your AT&T Stock?
detail:
If AT&T's Debt Stays High, What Happens To Your AT&T Stock?

Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

AT&T ended September with net debt at 3.13 times adjusted EBITDA, management's measure of earnings, up from 2.68 times in June. Management tied the increase to the spectrum licenses AT&T (T) bought from EchoStar at the end of July. The company expects to bring the ratio back to about 2.5 times during 2029, partly with money it has not yet received. If those funds arrive late, you would own a company carrying more debt for longer. So is the money for paying down that debt on its way?

AT&T Has Agreed Two Deals, But Neither Has Closed

The deals are agreed, but the money is not yet in hand. AT&T said on October 13 that it would sell AT&T Mexico to Grupo Televisa and Fintech Holdings. During its October 21 call, management described an agreement with Global Infrastructure Partners and CPP Investments to form a fiber joint venture. Management expects proceeds from both transactions in 2027, and plans to repay debt with those funds alongside spare cash and growth in earnings.

Carrying that debt is already costing more than management first planned. Cash interest payments for 2026 are running above the initial outlook, management said on the same call, mainly because of higher gross debt and interest rates. Until the two deals close, any debt AT&T repays will depend mainly on the cash its own business produces.

Shareholders Got Nearly All Of AT&T's Free Cash Flow

Over the twelve months to September, very little of that cash remained once shareholders were paid. AT&T generated $17.8 billion of free cash flow and paid $7.94 billion of it as dividends. Buybacks absorbed another $9.3 billion, bringing total payouts to $17.24 billion. Total debt rose to $178 billion over those twelve months, climbing from $158 billion a year earlier. Management still targets about $10 billion of buybacks for 2026, so spare cash for repaying debt stays small at that pace.

What Stuck Debt Would Cost An AT&T Holder

If the debt stays near today's level, AT&T's yearly interest bill is likely to be larger than the $7.47 billion of interest expense it recorded in the year to September. That period captured only two months of the higher debt load following the spectrum purchase at the end of July. AT&T's total debt also equals 121.9% of its market value, compared with 19.2% for the S&P 500. AT&T stock has also fallen harder than the market in a shock before: it dropped 20% from peak to low in the 2023 regional banking crisis, against 6.7% for the S&P 500.
